_what: How a computer of the person's speaks for Trillion in a natural voice made by a speech model on its own chip (computer/speak.mjs, run as tool:say-with-a-voice-model and tool:voices by computer/mac-tools.mjs, and by the Trillion Mac app to say notices out loud, macos/App/SpeakAloud.swift). Nothing goes to a paid service. `speech-program` rows (records/speech-engine-records.json, read through src/data-rows.mjs as `programs`) are the programs that run a speech model, tried in order the way computer-sources.json hearing rows are (the first whose `check` answers, its program found on `search_path`); `run` starts its resident speaker, which keeps each model loaded until it has been idle `speaker.idle_seconds` and answers on the socket `speaker.socket`. `speech-engine` rows (the same file, read as `engines`) are the speech models: `takes` says what makes the voice (a person's `reference` recording and its exact words, or a model's own `speaker`). `voices` are the voices every person has without making one, each kept as a row of the person's own Voices list the first time their voices are listed. A person's own voices, which voice they chose and every speed are rows of their own lists (src/voices.mjs: Voices, each { label, chosen, speed, engine, speaker, reference, reference_text, made_from, made_at }, and the places Trillion speaks), read through `person.tool` with their key (asked for at most `person.read_seconds`; each answer is kept on this computer as `person.kept` under `folder`, so a late or unreachable account never holds a sound up), with each reference recording in `person.folder` of their Trillion files, never here. A notice the Mac app could never make a sound for before it was too old to say is told once as failed work through `unsaid.tool` (key, kind, state and words in `unsaid`, filled with {notice}, {title}, {why} and {hours}), so it shows in the person's AI work with why. A sound is made at its natural pace and answered with the place's speed, which the player applies with the pitch kept. A voice is said with the voice asked for, else the person's chosen one, else each of `voices` in order; when none can run, the answer is an error and the caller tries again later (the Mac app never says a notice in its own system voice). `make` picks a reference from any recording of the person: the stretch, between `window.shortest_seconds` and `window.longest_seconds` long and nearest `window.best_seconds`, that starts after a pause and ends where a sentence ends with a pause after it, heard with `make.hear_model`, because a reference cut mid-sentence makes a model say its last words before the text. `loudness` brings every voice to one level. `keep` is where a said sound is kept in the person's files, so any of their devices plays it. A new voice is a row here; a new model or program is a row in records/speech-engine-records.json.

unsaid.title: Not said out loud: {title}
unsaid.body: This notice waited {hours} hours to be said out loud on this Mac, but its sound in your chosen voice could not be made, so it was never said. Why: {why}

words.too_long: That is more than {most} characters to say at once; split it.
words.no_program: This computer has no speech model program (mlx-audio), so it cannot make a natural voice.
words.no_voice: No voice could be made on this computer: {why}
words.unknown_voice: There is no voice {voice}. The voices are {voices}.
words.made: Your voice was made from {seconds} seconds of {name}: "{text}".
words.keeps_one: A voice every person has cannot be removed.
words.needs_recording: Give a recording of the person speaking (a file in their Trillion files) to make their voice from.
words.no_list: Your voices could not be read from your Trillion account just now, so nothing was changed. Try again in a minute.
